correctness.rationale: After each common purchase every balance remains (B-q)/n; the core price is 1/n and precedes any private candidate price of at least 1/n_j. The core ends at q=min(u,floor B). With the core exhausted, each petal has an isolated pool of n_j equally endowed supporters and purchases exactly min(|P_j|,floor(n_j(B-u)/n)) unit projects, ordered by fixed priority. Event thresholds are nondecreasing, proving the all-real-B nesting conclusion. Two ballots decompose as intersection and disjoint differences. The listed three-voter price sequence gives W(3)={A,B,C}, W(4)={A,B,D}, which is sharp in voter count because two-voter instances are always sunflower. The embedded exact rational verifier passed 156245 cases and explicit witness price traces. Infinite quantifiers follow from symbolic reasoning, not finite sample counts.

originality.rationale: The source paper on adaptive equal shares (arXiv:2310.10215v1) studies a distinct local-search rule and the motivation of virtual-budget changes, not the sunflower closed form. The strongest nearby theorem, Peters–Skowron laminar proportionality, is explicitly for fixed-size integral laminar instances and excludes the nonintegral party-list regime. The 2022 Lackner–Skowron book gives a four-voter failure of committee monotonicity, rather than a three-voter uncompleted-rule boundary. The general approval MES and variable-number-of-winners papers do not imply the new all-real-budget threshold law. Mathematical record comparisons and historical claim-level comparison produced no covering claim. This is a best-knowledge assessment with residual specialist priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: A more specialized or unindexed note might contain equivalent sunflower-case budget formulas or an independently earlier three-voter witness.
The older book Appendix A was available as extracted full text; a page-image fetch of that appendix was blocked, and no unsupported assertion about unread pages is made.
This claim does not assert tie-independent nonmonotonicity, a minimum number of candidates, or coverage of completion procedures.

value.rationale: The exact candidate-entry thresholds solve a motivated parametric budget-recomputation problem for arbitrary-size common-core/disjoint-interest approval populations: all project changes can be precomputed once as an ordered event list. The theorem identifies the boundary between stable and unstable budget paths at exactly three voters, sharpening the previously published four-voter witness specifically for the uncompleted purchase phase. The uncompleted/completed distinction and nonintegral quota scope prevent conflating the result with simpler fixed-committee laminar proportionality.
